'''Sound slugs''' were data storage units storing [[Music/Legends|musical]] recordings. The capacity of [[memory cell]]s and the efficiency of data compression techniques meant that a single slug the size of a [[Blaster power pack/Legends|blaster power pack]] could contain the entire catalog of even the most prolific artist, with spare capacity filled with [[Holovid/Legends|holovids]], reviews of the music, interviews with [[Band/Legends|band]] members, song lyrics, song remixes, technical analyses of the sound profiles, and more. These different [[Datafile/Legends|file]] types were stored in standardized formats, meaning the contents of a sound slug were readable on conventional [[Computer/Legends|computer]] systems, [[Datapad/Legends|datapads]], [[holovid machine]]s, and [[audio stack]]s. The cases containing them often featured decorative art,<ref name="GG9" /> and ninety percent of sound slugs used writing in the [[High Galactic/Legends|High Galactic alphabet]] on their covers, an example of that alphabet's dominance in galactic marketing.<ref name="Written Word">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/source/writtenword/index.html?page=1|text=The Written Word|int=The Written Word}}</ref>

Not all sound slugs held content beyond music, which meant a single slug had sufficient space to hold the entire music collection of its owner. The owner could expand their collection by buying a single musical track, typically for one to three [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]], or purchase a compilation of tracks such as an album at a discounted price, typically six to ten credits. A shop selling these tracks could download them onto a sound slug in a matter of seconds each.<ref name="GG9" />

As digital sound slugs grew in popularity, the ease with which they allowed the storage, selling, and trading of individual songs facilitated the exchange of popular music styles between [[Planet/Legends|worlds]], a phenomenon officially charted by [[Holomedia|news periodicals]] like [[HoloNet News/Legends|Holonet News]].<ref name="Slugthrowers1">{{SW|url=news/slugthrowers-an-overview-of-popular-music-and-musicians-in-a-galaxy-far-far-away-part-1|series=Slugthrowers: An Overview of Popular Music and Musicians in a Galaxy Far, Far Away|text=Part 1|nolive=1}}</ref>

The infamous killer [[Kardue'sai'Malloc/Legends|Kardue'sai'Malloc]] was an avid music collector, and when captured by the [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]], he made Fett promise to retrieve his priceless collection of sound slugs and [[music chip]]s and turn them over to the [[Director/Legends|director]] of the [[Coruscant University School of Music]], saving the work of hundreds of musicians who had been killed during the purges of the [[New Order/Legends|New Order]].<ref name="Slugthrowers2">{{SW|url=news/slugthrowers-part-2|series=Slugthrowers: An Overview of Popular Music and Musicians in a Galaxy Far, Far Away|text=Part 2|nolive=1}}</ref>
